s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with skin lesions in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
violaceous and crusted centers with purpura and edematous rings
key_facts: patient is a man in his late 60s
recent chemotherapy with ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone
tender skin lesions on the neck and trunk
skin biopsy shows inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138

raw.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with skin lesions in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
violaceous and crusted centers with purpura and edematous rings
key_facts: patient is a man in his late 60s
recent chemotherapy with ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone
tender skin lesions on the neck and trunk
skin biopsy shows inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fever, tender skin lesions, and laboratory findings such as a low white blood cell count and elevated C-reactive protein, along with the skin biopsy showing an inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells, are consistent with Sweet syndrome. The immunohistochemistry results, including positivity for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: While erythema multiforme can present with skin lesions, the specific pattern and the presence of fever and laboratory abnormalities in this case are more suggestive of Sweet syndrome.

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: There is no mention of respiratory symptoms or findings that would suggest Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.

rejected.label: Disseminated histoplasmosis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not specifically suggest histoplasmosis, and there is no mention of diagnostic tests for this condition.

rejected.label: Candidiasis
rejected.why: The skin biopsy and immunohistochemistry results do not support a diagnosis of candidiasis, which would typically involve fungal elements and different inflammatory patterns.
